4.30.betting_forecast: 4/6 Great Valley, 11/4 On Lovers Walk, 4/1 Franigane.
4.30.spotlight_verdict: With neither rival too frequent a front-runner, it takes little to imagine the down-in-trip GREAT VALLEY returning to the assertive tactics already deployed during his winning streak. Franigane's second to Barton Snow in this race last year reads even better now than it did then, but he wouldn't be the only competitor on this evening's card for whom the move from Cheltenham to Warwick doesn't strictly rate a plus. On Lovers Walk could ideally jump straighter. [Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: 33-1 into 18-1, flattered slightly by near-1l margin behind an idling Barton Snow in this race last year (good), but that was still a mighty run after 418 days out; absent again since, but his comparatively moderate RPRs around sharpish tracks probably concerns more.
horses.breeding: ch g Coastal Path - Nobless D'Aron

horses.spotlight_comment: Unbeaten in six since February 2025, encompassing 2m4f-3m contests around various track and going types; effortless transition to hunter chases at Ludlow latest (2m4f, good), and although patiently ridden there his proven ability at making all might yet come in handy down in trip.
horses.trainer: The Three O'Clock Fox N Gittins

horses.spotlight_comment: (7) 11-4 112 35 113 First wins for three years when striking last month in a Paxford restricted (2m4f) and Fakenham maiden hunter chase (3m, led last stride), both on good; prospects would improve if curbing the habit of jumping right evident on both of those occasions.
horses.trainer: Miss Kelly Morgan Miss K Morgan
horses.breeding: b g Walk In The Park - Hollygrove Samba

5.05.betting_forecast: Evs The Dancing Tree, 3/1 Mister Splash, 5/1 Practice Run, 6/1 Ultimate Survivor, 14/1 Fame And Concrete, 33/1
5.05.spotlight_verdict: Only Mister Splash has already contested a hunter chase, albeit nearly winning it. Alan Hill knows what he sends into this race, and a lack of experience of rules fences is of no more concern for the thriving THE DANCING TREE (nap) than it was his similarly profiled previous race winners Bon Accord, Harbour Court and Sharp Suit. Practice Run, representing the yard who won this in 2021, ran The Dancing Tree closest at Howick in March and can do so again here.[Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Both restricted wins in 2025 were recorded on good, which he's not encountered so far this campaign; interesting on that account, though no previous rules chasing experience and posted both his respective worst hurdle and bumper RPRs at Warwick.

Stamina to spare as a dual 3m4f winner, including at High Easter two runs ago, and effective on sound surfaces; can't afford a repeat of the jumps to the right of last month's Fakenham near-miss (chase debut).
horses.breeding: b g Court Cave - Bob's Flame

horses.spotlight_comment: No experience of rules fences, and has 6l to make up on The Dancing Tree judged on their Howick clash in March (soft); still on the up, however, making all in an intermediate at that same venue latest (good).

Dual 2025 point winner around stayers' tracks, and present season's best effort similarly came around Lockinge's galloping line last time, so may not appreciate Warwick as much as some; sound surface fine.

Ex-Gavin Cromwell; likely needed first run since April 2025 when beaten 28l on British/yard debut; middle leg of subsequent five-timer was a 6l defeat of Practice Run in a Howick intermediate (soft); untried over rules fences, but versatile as regards track and going types.

A length second but in turn well clear of Tellmesomethingood at Larkhill in December (good), and went one better there next time; didn't settle especially well on his first tilt at an intermediate latest, however, and brings zero rules experience with him.

5.40.betting_forecast: Evs Mister Coffey, 5/2 Alaphilippe, 11/4 What A Glance, 20/1 High Game Royal, 100/1 Laurel Girl.
5.40.spotlight_verdict: Retirement has already been delayed once for MISTER COFFEY in pursuit of that elusive chase win, and even allowing for an underwhelming hunter chase debut last time he'll surely never face another opportunity as good as tonight's. 2024 race winner What A Glance and one-time Prestige Hurdle scorer Alaphilippe possess the back class to trouble him, and the latter in particular arrives in good heart, but they will need to keep errors to a minimum. [Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Will have appreciated a simple task in his members race last time after a hard-fought Didmarton dead-heat; in better heart than many, but it's a worry that all bar one of his four chase starts have featured their share of jumping errors, including this race last year (pulled up).

Outpaced on all four starts this year, latterly in hunter chases at Stratford (2m5f) and Exeter (3m), on which evidence the marathon on this card might have been a more comfortable fit; others are more persuasive.
Over a fence behind last month when registering a first completion this campaign at the seventh attempt; impossible to fancy.

It was disappointing how far below form he ran when fourth switched to a hunter chase at Newbury latest (3m, good to soft), for all that it was a decent race of its type; even so, a repeat of the form of last November's Cheltenham second would still easily suffice in this thinner-looking race.
horses.trainer: Lady Bamford & Alice Bamford N Henderson

horses.spotlight_comment: Philipson-Stow (7) 11-4 134 - 132 Easy winner of this race in 2024 (soft) and the Stratford champion event (good) straight after, and nearest miss since when held by a neck at Brocklesby in February; there's always the chance he'll thrown in a mistake, but case is still good on this easiest-looking hunter chase assignment for some time.

6.15.betting_forecast: 2/1 Corporal Jackjones, 9/4 Imperial Esprit, 3/1 Kilfilum Woods, 4/1 Crawter.
6.15.spotlight_verdict: Crawter and KILFILUM WOODS will be glad to have no sight of the prolific pointer Grace A Vous Enki this evening, and the closer proximity in defeat of Kilfilum Woods to that rival, coupled with a bountiful spring in good-ground opens immediately beforehand, earns him preference. Corporal Jackjones (next best) may be best equipped to cope if this is run as an inadequate stamina test at the trip, while Imperial Esprit has his preferred ground and time of year.[Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: More than 5l too good in a Stratford novice hunter in March (2m5f, soft) despite whacking the last, and no shame since when second at Lower Machen giving the prolific Fumet d'Oudairies 3lb; could argue he's marginally more compelling at sub-3m trips, but among the likeliest even so.

Landed the intermediate on this card last term (good) despite his customary habit of jumping right; listless display at Exeter on his most recent hunter chase outing and had to work hard to land the odds in a 3m6f Larkhill open since (good to firm).

Exposed, but also placed in hunter chases on last three visits to Stratford (all sub-3m) and notably a winner during May in each of the previous three years; respected, for all that there's not huge substance to some of this spring's successes (two conditions events and a walkover).

Found only the prolific Grace A Vous Enki too good in the Lady Dudley Cup classic at Chaddesley Corbett last time (3m2f), having won two opens over shorter immediately before (all on good); first-fence casualty when last seen in a hunter chase, but generally a safe conveyance nowadays.

6.50.betting_forecast: 6/4 Police Academy, 4/1 Hollywood Harmon, 9/2 Walk Of No Shame, 6/1 All Loved Up, 12/1 For Rita, Missed Tee, 14/1 Loud And
6.50.spotlight_verdict: Representing the Kelly Morgan operation which took this race in 2022 with Feuille De Lune and struck twice in hunter chases only last month, POLICE ACADEMY is taken to carry the revived cheer from two recent open point wins back to a rules track. There are reasons to approach Walk Of No Shame and Loud And Proud with a little trepidation, earning the stamina-laden All Loved Up preference as next best. [Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Enjoying her most productive season to date, last month's Kimble open point win (good to firm) making it three wins from four; stamina to spare (won the 3m6f Lord Ashton of Hyde classic) and no shock if she goes closer than last year's 24l fourth in this contest.

Most realistic assignment of the year when taking a Kingston Blount hands-and-heels race latest (good), in the process posting a win for the sixth straight pointing season; acts on all going, but the form of her two previous hunter chase efforts (almost three years apart) doesn't pass muster.

125-1 and never a factor at Aintree last time; won't find it as hard to adopt her preferred position at or near the early speed here, but barely stays 3m (sole win at that trip came at Askham Bryan's very sharp circuit) and has further still to go here.

Easily won a 3m2f Doncaster mares' handicap in March 2025 for Harry Derham (good) and denied only close home in points at Revesby Park (3m) and Bangor-on-Dee (2m4f) this year; have to hope last-time failure doesn't presage a return to last autumn's rules struggles, however.
Third and sixth in the last two renewals of the 2m race on this card, and still appeals more over shorter despite a win over the full 3m trip at Chaddesley Corbett last May; 0-14 over rules fences.
horses.trainer: Miss Sarah A Dawson Miss V Collins
horses.breeding: b m Walk In The Park - Ultimate Echo

horses.spotlight_comment: Unlucky to lose last June's Uttoxeter chase win (3m, good) on a medical technicality; wheels came off in the autumn but she has revived for current yard, keeping on well for Higham and High Easter open successes on good to firm; could prove the answer.

Close third of three in a Dunsmore open (good to soft) on her most recent pointing start, but her quirkier side was also evident this year having run out under two different riders; risks attached therefore, and she offered nothing on a sole previous chasing start (3m, 0-120) in autumn 2024.

7.25.betting_forecast: Evs Jeffery's Cross, 4/1 Slipway, 5/1 Peaches And Cream, 13/2 Myth Buster, 7/1 My Gift To You.
7.25.spotlight_verdict: None can be safely ruled out. Last year's runner-up Jeffery's Cross has had six weeks to recover from a hard-fought Newbury success, and the move from Cheltenham to Warwick is no negative. A chance is nevertheless taken on PEACHES AND CREAM, set an easier assignment than is usually the case when stepped up to a marathon trip, and already off the mark in points for his new connections. My Gift To You should give his usual honest account. [Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Beaten under 1l in this race last year (Myth Buster pulled up); won't mind the move from Cheltenham given his strong body of work around sharp tracks (including 2-2 in hurdles races here, albeit losing one for interference), and nice break since hard-fought Newbury win; ground fine.
horses.trainer: Spectre Racing - Jeffrey's Cross D Skelton

horses.spotlight_comment: Highly impressive 26 finishes in the first four (eight of them wins) from 30 rules/pointing runs for the Owens, with stamina proven up to 3m6f; all-the-way hurdles winner over 3m2f here just last autumn (good), and likelier than some to run his race.

Possibly softened up by the pace battle when pulling up in this race last year (28-1), but generally a sound stayer and has made every yard in his two most recent points (good, good to soft); chance as long as Lily Bradstock, who knows him so well, can keep him interested.

Punchestown 3m7f handicap chase win in April 2022 (good) remains his most recent under rules, but the first of two point starts netted him a last-gasp Bangor-on-Dee success in March; strike-rate of only 1-11 over 3m3f or more, but this would be easier than almost any of those.

Former winner of Highland and Southern Nationals (good to soft), so surprising he didn't see out 3m here on January's hunter chase debut; back on track in a Siddington novice riders' point latest, additionally a first career success on good ground; safe ride (never falls) and not dismissed.

8.00.betting_forecast: 2/5 Unexpected Party, 5/1 Fan De Blues, 7/1 Arthur's Sixpence, 14/1 Empire De Maulde, 20/1 Hystery Bere.
8.00.spotlight_verdict: Still able to record a respectable fourth - and in the process reaffirm Taunton superiority over the reopposing Fan De Blues - in the Aintree Foxhunters despite bleeding from the nose, a completely sound UNEXPECTED PARTY won't be hard pressed to vindicate Dan Skelton's choosing of him over two stablemates from the initial race entry. [Jeremy Grayson]

horses.spotlight_comment: Fine effort at 150-1 when under 3l third at Newbury in March; all wins in the last four years, including matches in two opens in 2025, gained going left-handed on sound/quick surfaces, and perhaps best forgiven an uncharacteristic exit at Lockinge latest as he usually finds a leg.

Victory in a Parham open match last weekend took his score in points to 5-8; diminishing returns in hunter chases, and well held behind Arthur's Sixpence at Newbury in March (3m, good to soft), albeit on going which wouldn't have suited as well as tonight's projected good.

Wind surgery has largely got him back on track this year, and there's surely a sub-3m hunter chase in him; 9l behind Unexpected Party at Aintree latest, having been beaten half that distance by him at Taunton in January (2m6f, good), and likely needs that old rival to underperform.
horses.trainer: Miss Nikki Henton Miss N Henton
horses.breeding: b g Pedro The Great - Mysteryonthebounty

horses.spotlight_comment: 2m novice handicap winner here three years ago to the day (good; RPR 129), and several decent placed efforts after; able schoolmaster for Joe Neal in novice rider points lately, getting there in time at Kimble (3m, good to firm) but not quite last time; others a bit more persuasive.

Bled from the nose when a fading fourth in the Aintree Foxhunters latest (2m5f, good to soft), though still had Fan De Blues comfortably behind for the second time this year; more prolific on easier surfaces but Taunton win in January reaffirmed he's effective on good as well.
horses.trainer: O'Reilly Maclennan Tynan Carthy Shanahan D Skelton
horses.breeding: b g Spanish Moon - Ondine De Brejoux
